questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about a connected graph?

options.text: Every vertex is connected to every other vertex by a path.
Every vertex has an even degree.
The graph contains an Euler circuit.
The graph contains a Hamiltonian cycle.

questions.explanation: A connected graph is defined by the existence of a path between every pair of vertices. This does not imply anything about the degrees of vertices or the existence of Euler circuits or Hamiltonian cycles.

questions.stem: A graph has vertices \( A, B, C, D \) with degrees \( 2, 3, 3, 2 \) respectively. Does this graph have an Euler path?

options.text: Yes, because it is connected and has exactly two vertices of odd degree.
No, because it is not connected.
Yes, because all vertices have even degree.
No, because it has more than two vertices of odd degree.

questions.explanation: An Euler path exists if a graph is connected and has exactly two vertices of odd degree. Here, vertices \( B \) and \( C \) have odd degrees, satisfying the condition.

questions.explanation: A graph with 5 vertices and 4 edges can be connected if the edges form a tree. However, if it is not connected, it can have multiple components. With 4 edges, it can form a tree with 5 vertices or two components with 3 and 2 vertices respectively.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions guarantees the existence of an Euler circuit in a graph?

options.text: The graph is connected and all vertices have even degree.
The graph is connected and has exactly two vertices of odd degree.
The graph is connected and has at least one vertex of odd degree.
The graph is connected and all vertices have odd degree.

questions.explanation: An Euler circuit exists in a graph if and only if the graph is connected and all vertices have even degree. This ensures that each edge can be traversed exactly once, returning to the starting vertex.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between an Euler path and a Hamiltonian path.
markingGuide: Euler path uses every edge exactly once.
Hamiltonian path visits every vertex exactly once.
Euler paths focus on edges, Hamiltonian paths focus on vertices.
Conditions for existence differ: Euler paths require specific vertex degrees, Hamiltonian paths have no simple condition.
questions.explanation: Euler paths and Hamiltonian paths differ primarily in their focus: Euler paths require each edge to be used exactly once, while Hamiltonian paths require each vertex to be visited exactly once. The conditions for their existence also differ, with Euler paths having specific requirements on vertex degrees, while Hamiltonian paths lack a simple necessary and sufficient condition.

questions.stem: What is a connected component in a graph?

options.text: A subgraph in which any two vertices are connected by a path.
A subgraph containing all vertices of even degree.
A subgraph that contains a Hamiltonian cycle.
A subgraph that contains an Euler circuit.

questions.explanation: A connected component is a maximal subgraph in which any two vertices are connected by a path. It is the largest connected subgraph within a graph.

questions.stem: Describe a method to determine if a given graph has an Euler circuit.
markingGuide: Check if the graph is connected.
Verify that all vertices have even degree.

questions.explanation: To determine if a graph has an Euler circuit, first check if the graph is connected, meaning there is a path between every pair of vertices. Then, verify that all vertices have even degree. Both conditions must be satisfied for the existence of an Euler circuit.
